title: Perf run 20261021-2131
heading: Checks for the build and the piece data, and a tutorial that says when its board failed
meta: This general run kept 15 changes, none made for speed. Six are new checks: the build runs every plugin its config defines, the piece data loads again after a failed load and every page that draws pieces loads it, the lobby's king builds without it, the built page's early socket script is run as the browser runs it, the early pictures' scripts go into the page as written, and the lobby's occlusion split is pinned to the king. Five fix bugs: a computer game left before its page arrived no longer opens with an arrival later, the preloads follow the whole chunk graph, the tutorial says when its board or its page did not load, with a Retry, and a narrowed A/B no longer speaks for rows it never measured. Four replace copies with one source: the field of view, the tutorial card's gutter, the occlusion's king-and-the-rest split and the computer's "search did not load" reply. The one speed idea tried (PD2) made two boards' first pictures 18–29% slower and was reverted. On the final commit, measured against the base 91b2081 over 10 pairs, no primary row is called better or worse, and a re-check of the rows that leaned calls nothing either. The branch is improve/20261021-2131; main did not move during the run. Every figure comes from software rendering (SwiftShader) on a 4-vCPU VM, and each one names the commits it compares.

needs.intro: Nothing here needs a decision. The items are information that the speed rule asks for.

items.title: Four primary rows lean worse in one A/B or the other; none is called
items.body:
Information, not a question. The speed rule lists any primary row that is more than 3% worse at the median pair. The final A/B (ab-20261021-2131-final.md) listed three. A re-check of their two sections, setup and move latency, 10 pairs (ab-20261021-2131-final-recheck.md), on the same app, gave:

  • The opponent's move appears: ×1.055 (6 of 10 pairs worse), then ×1.082 (7 of 10, pairs 0.95–1.42).
  • First board picture, joining a game: ×1.012 (6 of 10), then ×1.042 (8 of 10, pairs 0.94–1.11).
  • A shared game's page, first screen, desktop: ×1.074 (8 of 10), then ×0.957 (3 of 10).
  • The player's move appears: ×1.128 (6 of 10), then ×0.990 (5 of 10).

The branch changes nothing that runs per move. On the board's first build it adds one includes on a one-item list per piece type. The move rows swing by about 10% between A/Bs of the same code: last run's opponent's move leaned ×1.04 twice, and this run's step 2 read it ×0.938 on that same app.

items.title: The picked-up piece's lean is noise
items.body: Information, not a question. "A picked-up piece appears" leaned ×1.068 and ×1.095 on the base against the last run's base. An A/A of identical code (select, 12 pairs, ab-20261021-2131-select-aa.md) read it ×1.048, with 8 of 12 pairs worse. In the final A/B it reads ×1.007.

charts.caption: The A/A: select, 9d25de2 against itself, 12 pairs (ab-20261021-2131-select-aa.md).

scoreboard.intro: The primary rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. Each bar is a row's change, head divided by base, and each dot is one pair. Left of 1× is faster. The dashed line is the target, 1.2× faster than the base.

items.title: The final commit against the base: all 20 primary rows
items.body:
2c29fb9 against 91b2081, 10 pairs, 80 minutes (ab-20261021-2131-final.md). The later commits change only the loop's records. Overall the head is ×0.992 as fast as the base, against ×1.004 for identical code. No primary row and none of the 123 diagnostics is called. Every load downloads the same bytes as on the base. Memory is flat: the JS heap after reopening a 2,000-ply game went from 14,607.4 to 14,532.3 KiB (−0.3%), and live geometries and textures did not change.

The 1.2× target is not met: no row is faster. This general run made no change for speed, and its one speed idea (PD2) was rejected.

items.title: The base against the last run's base
items.body: Step 2: 91b2081 against 9ca180a, 10 pairs, 81 minutes (ab-20261021-2131-regress.md). This is the same app that run 1153's final A/B measured. Two rows are called better again: a shared game's first screen on a phone, 876 → 697 ms (×0.801), and reopening a game against the computer on a phone, 1.40 s → 740 ms (×0.525). Nothing is called worse. The JS heap after reopening a 2,000-ply game went from 14,665.0 to 14,621.0 KiB (−0.3%).

items.title: The long view: against the first recorded run
items.body: Not measured again in this run. The last measurement, from run 20261018-1719, compares 8a3e922 with the first recorded run 92ce041 over 3 pairs.

changed.intro: Each change is its own commit. Every check below was shown to fail on a broken copy of the code, or on the base 91b2081, and to pass on the branch. Each commit message says how the code was broken.

items.title: The tutorial says when its board did not load (f6cd129)
items.body: Before, when the board's code, the piece data or WebGL failed on /learn, the stage stayed empty and the card said nothing. Now the card's foot says "Couldn't load the board" with a Retry, or "No 3D board: WebGL is off in this browser". These are the game's own words. A second failure reloads the page, as on a game's page. Three new tests fail on the base.

items.title: The tutorial's page offers a Retry when it did not load (f5b9ddc)
items.body: When the tutorial's own code failed to load, the page said so but offered only Home. It now offers Retry, which reloads the page, as a game's page does. A test that clicks Retry fails on the base.

items.title: A computer game left early no longer opens with an arrival later (157569c)
items.body: The side choice marked a new computer game as arriving before its page's code had loaded. A player who left during that wait left the game marked, so a later visit played the arrival again. The mark is now set only when the page actually opens. A new test fails on the base.

items.title: Preloads follow the whole chunk graph (d7c5550)
items.body: The build's per-page preload list looked only one import deep. It now follows every chunk a page's chunks import, using one walk that the build's own guard shares. The plugin is renamed preload-route-chunks. A two-level test fails on the base. Today this adds two small files (2.3 KB and 147 B) to /learn's low-priority list; the other pages' lists are unchanged by a local diff of the built pages. No primary row measures /learn.

items.title: New checks on the build and the piece data
items.body:
• 7d361c9: every plugin vite.config.ts defines must be in its plugins list.
  • a2909a4: the piece data loads again after a failed load, and every page that draws pieces loads it.
  • 22dfe6a: the lobby's king builds without the piece data, and the other pieces refuse to.
  • 9d25de2: the built page's early socket script is run, for each address, not only read.
  • 3638a7f: the early pictures' scripts go into the page as written, even with $& in them. This is the check for d7c5550's change to a function replacer, which had none.
  • 25ba199: the lobby's occlusion split is pinned to the king alone. With the queen added and the data baked again, only this test fails.
  • c39b024: a narrowed A/B report no longer says "no primary row is worse" about rows it never measured.

items.title: One source instead of copies
items.body:
• 5b863c8: CAMERA_FOV, one field of view for every canvas and the lobby's last pose, with a check.
  • f2b0ccc: the tutorial card's gutter is the start page's, and its stylesheet's copy is checked.
  • 51bb1ad: the occlusion's king-and-the-rest split is named once for the bake, the scene and the test. The bake rewrites the generated files byte for byte.
  • 59ecc89: one place for the computer's "search did not load" reply.

removed.intro: No file or dependency was removed. Without tests, the client and the bench runner gained 156 lines and lost 103, a net 53 lines: mostly the tutorial's failure notice and its Retry. The preload plugin's three graph walks became one, and the hooks layer went from 723 to 718 lines.

rejected.intro: Ideas tried or probed and not kept:

items.title: PD2: start the piece data later on the side choice, and from the head on game pages
items.body: Measured against f6cd129 on the setup and computer sections, 8 pairs (ab-20261021-2131-pd2.md). Joining's first picture went from 858 ms to 1.01 s (×1.178) and the computer's first picture from 895 ms to 1.14 s (×1.290), both called worse in 8 of 8 pairs. The side choice's scene on a phone went from 2.23 s to 2.17 s (×0.978), not called. Reverted; its patch is bench/loop/patches/2131-PD2.patch. A variant stays in the ledger: start the data after the lobby's first frame.

charts.caption: PD2 against f6cd129, setup and computer, 8 pairs (ab-20261021-2131-pd2.md).

items.title: One helper for the four inline scripts in the page's head
items.body: Tried: 18 more lines after formatting, with no change in behaviour. Not kept. Parked until a fifth inline script exists.

items.title: Early Hints and Link headers for the preloads (EH1)
items.body: Rejected on reading, not measured. Cloudflare Pages builds Link headers only from <link> tags without crossorigin, the preloads come from a script, and static pages leave no server time for a 103 to fill.

items.title: Where the tutorial says its board failed
items.body: In the card's foot, where the move count stands, in the game's words, with a text Retry like Reset. A notice over the stage would change the card's height.

items.title: Kept the preload change without its own A/B
items.body: It changes only /learn's low-priority links, which no primary row measures. The final A/B covers the rest.

items.title: Parked the picked-piece lean (PK1)
items.body: "A picked-up piece appears" leaned ×1.068 and ×1.095 on the base. An A/A of identical code read it ×1.048 with 8 of 12 pairs worse (ab-20261021-2131-select-aa.md), so the leans are within the row's own spread.

items.title: Fixed two review findings instead of logging them
items.body: d7c5550's function replacer had no test that could fail; 3638a7f adds one. 51bb1ad had made the king-only test compare a constant with itself; 25ba199 pins it again. ARCHITECTURE.md now says what the tutorial shows when it fails to load.

items.title: The built pages' preload lists
items.body: That the /, /game, /new and /computer lists are unchanged comes from a local diff of the two builds that is not in the repo (ledger 2131:BP1).

items.title: Production's HTTP/2 and 3
items.body: Every phone row runs over HTTP/1.1 from vite preview (ledger 1153:H2). PD2's result may differ there.

items.title: The tutorial's Retry in Firefox and Safari
items.body: Checked only in Chromium, which keeps a failed module failed until a reload (ledger 2131:CR1).

items.title: 1153:H2: run the phone rows over HTTP/2
items.body: Serve the bench over TLS and HTTP/2, as production does, before more preload work. PD2's result shows how far HTTP/1.1 can mislead.

items.title: PD2's variant, SL1, SH1, CH1
items.body: Start the piece data after the lobby's first frame; overlap the lobby's shader links with building its scene; draw the at-rest shimmer from a copy; retry V8 compile hints.

items.title: 2131:LB1 and 2131:NF1
items.body: A primary row for the tutorial's first board frame, and a verdict that judges each row against its own A/A spread.

items.title: General: 2131:LQ1, BR1, FP1, SS1, 1153:DF1's e2e half, UM1's remainder
items.body: A status line when the game's page is slow after the pick (measure first), one board-retry hook and one failed-page component, sturdier source-scan checks, an e2e of the piece data failing, and the scoreboard's count of unmeasured rows.
